## E1 — Detection accuracy

Not run. The E1 harness is in place (`src/rulecam/eval/manifests.py`,
`eval/runners/e1.py`, `eval/report.py`), but no measured run exists, because it needs the recordings (S-03) and a
consented manifest. `uv run python -c "from eval.report import write_results_section, ..."`
replaces everything between these two markers; nothing else in this file is touched.

Before a run can happen: the clips must be recorded, every person in them must have signed a
consent form (`docs/consent.md`), and the manifest must name each form. A clip without a form is
refused outright, so no number here can come from footage nobody agreed to.

<!-- END E1 -->

### Correction (Oct 31): E3 figures withdrawn

This file previously reported E3 as 100.0% valid-or-honest (60/60), 96.7% first-pass acceptance,
0.03 repair rounds and 0.90 s per plan. Those figures came from `eval/runners/e3.py`, a simulated
harness that does not call the Planner:

- declines came from the real deterministic guardrail;
- "not observable" outcomes were copied from each request's own `expected_outcome` label;
- every other request received the same fixed `inside` rule;
- durations and repair rounds were set in code, not measured.

The numbers were therefore true by construction. They, the 60 plans in `plans/heldout/` and
`eval/results/e3.json` have been removed. The 20 requests in `eval/heldout/requests.jsonl` were
written by the team as personas, not by outside authors as S-04 requires, and are now labelled
that way.

A real E3 needs two things: the Planner pipeline in place of `simulate_plan_for_request`, and
requests written by people outside the team (W-10 in `reports/Rulecam next 1`). Until then the
runner marks its output `simulated=True` and can never pass the E3 gate.
